stages.headline: Inductive reasoning goes from particular cases to a general conclusion; it can be wrong, so the conclusion must be proved.
stages.headlineEnglish: Inductive reasoning goes from particular cases to a general conclusion; it can be wrong, so the conclusion must be proved.

stages.headline: n² + n + 41 is prime for n = 0, 1, …, 39, but for n = 40 it equals 41², a composite number.
stages.headlineEnglish: n² + n + 41 is prime for n = 0, 1, …, 39, but for n = 40 it equals 41², a composite number.

stages.headline: Complete induction checks all (finitely many) cases and is reliable; incomplete induction checks only some of them.
stages.headlineEnglish: Complete induction checks all (finitely many) cases and is reliable; incomplete induction checks only some of them.
